chunks: From him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Bariqi, from Abu Ali ibn Rashid, from Ibrahim ibn al-Sindi, from Yunus ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I described to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) those who proclaim this matter [the Imamate] who work with the Sultan. He said: 'When they appoint you, they insert the elbow [press their advantage] and benefit you in your needs.' I said: 'Among them are some who do this, and some who do not.' He said: 'So for those among them who do not do that, disavow them, and Allah will disavow them.'

key_terms.ابْرَءُوا مِنْهُ: Disavow him / declare innocence from him
key_terms.الْمَرْفِقَ: The elbow (idiom for pressing advantage or inserting oneself)

ai.seo_question: What is the criterion for disavowing those who claim leadership while serving the ruler?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a criterion for evaluating the legitimacy of claimants to the Imamate who serve under political rulers, emphasizing that their utility to the community is a key indicator of their standing. He distinguishes between those who actively benefit the people and those who do not, prescribing a mutual disavowal (bara'ah) between Allah and the people for the latter, reflecting the Shia concept of political pragmatism coupled with spiritual discernment. This narration underscores the importance of tangible service to the community as a metric for validating religious authority in the context of the minor and major occultations.
